1	# The Nexus bench — `internal/nexusbench`
2	
3	> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
4	> read this file when working on the code it describes.
5	
6	## What it is
7	
8	DEVDESK-504 (NX-01): a disposable Nexus Community instance on the k0s cluster
9	of `datomir`, deployed, provisioned over REST and destroyed with one command, so
10	the registry measurements of the NX stories run against a real Nexus. It is a
11	development tool: the `dk` binary does not import it, nothing in `mise run
12	check` or `mise run ci` touches a cluster, and integration tests skip unless
13	`DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH=1` is set (and always when `CI` is set).
14	
15	Status: the parameters (step 1), the manifest rendering (step 2), the `kubectl`
16	runner, errors and preflight (step 3), the deployment and its wait (step 4), the
17	secrets store and the descriptor (step 5), the REST client and provisioning
18	(step 6), the destruction (step 7), the command with its mise tasks (step 8) and
19	the guarded integration tests with the source guards (step 9) exist. The
20	preflight only reads the cluster; the writes are the two applies of `Deploy`,
21	the REST calls of `Provision` and the namespace delete of `Destroy`.
22	
23	Validated on `datomir` on 2026-11-16 (step 10, see "First real run" below): `up`,
24	a second `up`, the three read-only integration tests and the destructive
25	lifecycle all ran against a real Nexus 3.98.1-01 Community on k0s. One
26	hypothesis was wrong (a proxy whose upstream does not resolve is refused), and
27	`Provision` now copes with it.
28	
29	## Decisions (plan `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-504-plan.md`)
30	
31	- **D-A** A Go package, `internal/nexusbench`, with a `package main` under
32	  `cmd/nexus-bench`, driven by `mise run nexus-bench:*` tasks outside `ci`.
33	  `kubectl` through `os/exec`, no `client-go`, no bash.
34	- **D-B** Namespace `nexus-bench`, context `datomir`, NodePorts 30481 (REST,
35	  UI) and 30482 (Docker connector); 30483-30489 reserved for the next NX
36	  stories. Refused: namespaces `default`, `kube-*`, `app-*`, `flux-system`,
37	  `local-path-storage`, `traefik`, `kyverno`, `observability`, `plane`; NodePorts
38	  outside 30000-32767 or equal; an image from `tvp-zot.incus:5000` (Kyverno
39	  `verify-tvp-images` admits signed images only).
40	- **D-C** Resources 500m/2 CPU, 3Gi/4Gi memory, 5Gi PVC, JVM 1 GiB heap and 1 GiB
41	  direct memory, image `docker.io/sonatype/nexus3:3.98.1`. To be confirmed on
42	  the first real run (H-RES).
43	- **D-D** A deterministic, versioned `descriptor.json` (no timestamp, pod name or
44	  secret); secrets in a `0600` file outside the repository, shared by all
45	  worktrees.
46	- **D-E** Idempotent REST provisioning: read, then create or replace; admin
47	  password changed with the new one written first; the EULA is accepted only
48	  with `NEXUS_BENCH_ACCEPT_EULA=yes`.
49	- **D-F** One typed error with a cause and a check to run; the preflight runs
50	  before any write; the namespace carries a `managed-by` label and `down`
51	  refuses to delete one without it.
52	
53	## Parameters (`params.go`)
54	
55	Precedence: flag, then `NEXUS_BENCH_*` variable, then default. `FromEnv(base,
56	getenv)` applies the variables onto `base` and returns a new value (the base is
57	not changed); an empty variable counts as unset; a value that does not parse is
58	an error naming its variable. `Validate()` runs before any call to the cluster
59	and reports every problem at once. Every value that reaches a manifest is
60	checked against a strict pattern, newlines included. The patterns are meant to
61	keep a value from injecting YAML on their own, but the templates still
62	writes every value quoted: the validation is the first guard, not the only one.
63	
64	| Field | Variable | Default |
65	|---|---|---|
66	| `Context` | `NEXUS_BENCH_CONTEXT` | `datomir` |
67	| `Namespace` | `NEXUS_BENCH_NAMESPACE` | `nexus-bench` |
68	| `HTTPNodePort` | `NEXUS_BENCH_HTTP_NODEPORT` | `30481` |
69	| `DockerNodePort` | `NEXUS_BENCH_DOCKER_NODEPORT` | `30482` |
70	| `CPURequest` / `CPULimit` | `NEXUS_BENCH_CPU_REQUEST` / `_CPU_LIMIT` | `500m` / `2` |
71	| `MemoryRequest` / `MemoryLimit` | `NEXUS_BENCH_MEMORY_REQUEST` / `_MEMORY_LIMIT` | `3Gi` / `4Gi` |
72	| `StorageSize` | `NEXUS_BENCH_STORAGE_SIZE` | `5Gi` |
73	| `JVMOpts` | `NEXUS_BENCH_JVM_OPTS` | `-Xms1g -Xmx1g -XX:MaxDirectMemorySize=1g -Djava.util.prefs.userRoot=/nexus-data/javaprefs` |
74	| `Image`, `ImageTag` | `NEXUS_BENCH_IMAGE`, `_IMAGE_TAG` | `docker.io/sonatype/nexus3`, `3.98.1` |
75	| `UpstreamImage`, `UpstreamImageTag` | `NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_IMAGE`, `_UPSTREAM_IMAGE_TAG` | `docker.io/library/registry`, `3.0.0` |
76	| `UpstreamURL` | `NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_URL` | `http://bench-upstream.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local:5000` |
77	| `Anonymous` | `NEXUS_BENCH_ANONYMOUS` | `true` |
78	| `AcceptEULA` | `NEXUS_BENCH_ACCEPT_EULA` | `false`; true only for the exact value `yes` |
79	| `Hosts` | `NEXUS_BENCH_HOSTS` (comma list) | none: derived (`127.0.0.1`, node InternalIP) |
80	| `Timeout`, `DeleteTimeout` | `NEXUS_BENCH_TIMEOUT`, `_DELETE_TIMEOUT` | `10m`, `3m` |
81	| `SecretsPath`, `DescriptorPath` | `NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS`, `NEXUS_BENCH_DESCRIPTOR` | none: derived |
82	
83	Rules beyond the shape of each value:
84	
85	- CPU, memory and storage quantities are greater than zero (`0`, `0m`, `0Gi` are
86	  refused), and a request never exceeds its limit (CPU compared in milli-cores,
87	  memory in bytes, units mixed freely: `2000m` equals `2`). The error names both
88	  variables, so a lone `NEXUS_BENCH_MEMORY_LIMIT=2Gi` against the default `3Gi`
89	  request is refused.
90	- `JVMOpts` is 1-512 characters among letters, digits, space and `_ . , : = / + @ %
91	  -`; it starts with a letter, a digit, or `-` followed by a non-space (so not
92	  `- x`, `@x`, `%x`, `,x`, `:x`), holds no `": "` and does not end with `:`, so it is
93	  a plain YAML scalar by itself.
94	- `Hosts` entries are IP addresses or host names (letters, digits, `.`, `-`,
95	  253 characters at most): no port, no whitespace.
96	- `UpstreamURL` is `http://` or `https://` plus a host, without credentials, made
97	  of URL characters only (no `@`, no whitespace) and with a port, when present,
98	  between 1 and 65535.
99	- `Image`/`ImageTag` and `UpstreamImage`/`UpstreamImageTag` go through one
100	  `validateImage(imageEnv, tagEnv, image, tag)`: each error names the variable of
101	  its own pair. Both refuse the `tvp-zot.incus:5000` prefix (Kyverno
102	  `verify-tvp-images`, unsigned bench images).
103	- `UpstreamImageRef()` is `UpstreamImage:UpstreamImageTag`. `UpstreamIsBench()` is
104	  true when `UpstreamURL` is the in-cluster URL of `Namespace`, i.e. the bench
105	  deploys its own upstream rather than pointing the proxy at a custom one.
106	- The CLI flags `--upstream-image` and `--upstream-image-tag` are common flags; a
107	  non-default value makes `describesDefaultBench` false (descriptor not to be
108	  committed).
109	- Paths hold no control character and are 4096 bytes at most.
110	
111	`NEXUS_BENCH_NAMESPACE` alone moves `UpstreamURL` to the new namespace, unless
112	the base already carried a custom upstream or `NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_URL` is set.
113	The context name is limited to letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `@` and `-`, because
114	it names a directory of the secrets path.
115	
116	## Manifests (`render.go`, `manifests/`)
117	
118	`Render(p Params) ([]byte, error)` calls `p.Validate()` first (an invalid value
119	returns Validate's error, naming its variable, and no bytes) and writes a
120	multi-document YAML stream separated by `---`, in this order: Namespace, PVC,
121	Deployment, Service (Nexus), then PVC, Deployment, Service (the upstream
122	registry): seven documents. `RenderNamespace(p)` returns the first document alone, so
123	that `up` can apply the Namespace before the rest. The output is deterministic
124	(no map iteration, no timestamp); the golden of the defaults is
125	`testdata/render-default.golden.yaml`, rewritten with
126	`go test ./internal/nexusbench -run TestRenderGolden -update` and reviewed as a
127	diff.
128	
129	| File (`go:embed`, `text/template`) | Object |
130	|---|---|
131	| `00-namespace.yaml.tmpl` | Namespace, labels `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by` and `part-of` = `devdesk-nexus-bench`; no `pod-security.kubernetes.io/*` label |
132	| `10-pvc.yaml.tmpl` | PVC `nexus-data`, `ReadWriteOnce`, `StorageSize`, no `storageClassName` (the cluster default class, `local-path`) |
133	| `20-deployment.yaml.tmpl` | Deployment `nexus`: 1 replica, `Recreate`, one container (`ImageRef`), ports `http` 8081 and `docker-group` 8082, requests and limits, env `INSTALL4J_ADD_VM_PARAMS`, PVC on `/nexus-data`, `startupProbe` on `/service/rest/v1/status` (10 s x 60 = 10 min), `readinessProbe` (same path), no `livenessProbe`, UID and GID 200, `runAsNonRoot`, no privilege escalation, `drop: [ALL]`, `RuntimeDefault` seccomp, no service account token, no service links |
134	| `30-service.yaml.tmpl` | Service `nexus`, `NodePort`: `http` 8081 to `HTTPNodePort`, `docker-group` 8082 to `DockerNodePort` |
135	| `40-upstream-pvc.yaml.tmpl` | PVC `bench-upstream-data`, `ReadWriteOnce`, a fixed `1Gi` (`StorageSize` sizes Nexus only), no `storageClassName`; label `app.kubernetes.io/name: bench-upstream` on the three upstream objects |
136	| `50-upstream-deployment.yaml.tmpl` | Deployment `bench-upstream`: **no `replicas` field** (`kubectl scale` owns it, so a server-side apply of the whole stream neither conflicts with it nor puts the upstream back after it was cut), `Recreate`, one container (`UpstreamImageRef`), port `registry` 5000, env `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=none` (distribution v3 traces by default), fixed requests 50m / 64Mi and limits 500m / 256Mi, PVC on `/var/lib/registry`, `readinessProbe` `GET /v2/`, UID and GID 1000, `runAsNonRoot`, no privilege escalation, `drop: [ALL]`, `RuntimeDefault` seccomp, no service account token, no service links |

139	Quoting: the templates see only a `manifestData` built from validated values,
140	and every string goes through the `q` template function (`strconv.Quote`, a
141	valid YAML double-quoted scalar), so `true`, `null`, `123`, `0x1F`, `12:30:45` or
142	`2001-01-23` in `NEXUS_BENCH_JVM_OPTS` decode as strings (`TestRenderRoundTripsTrickyJVMOpts`,
143	`TestRenderQuotesEveryValue`). Quoted: namespace, image references (Nexus and upstream), JVM options,
144	CPU and memory quantities, storage size, and the fixed values of the upstream
145	documents. Not quoted: the two NodePorts (integers),
146	and the literals of the template (names, labels, container ports).
147	
148	What the render does not carry: the context, the upstream URL, `Anonymous`,
149	`AcceptEULA`, `Hosts`, timeouts and paths (a change of any of them leaves the
150	bytes unchanged, `TestRenderIgnoresParamsTheManifestsDoNotCarry`); no Secret, no
151	ConfigMap, no `envFrom` or `valueFrom`, no hostPath, no object of cluster scope
152	but the Namespace; the word `password` or `secret` never appears. The admin
153	password is read from the pod and written to the secrets file by the
154	provisioning step, not by a manifest.

156	## Errors, runner and preflight (`errors.go`, `kubectl.go`, `preflight.go`)
157	
158	**Errors.** Every failure of the bench is a `*BenchError{Kind, Cause, Check, Err}`.
159	`Error()` is `"<Cause>. Check: <Check>"`: a probable cause and what to run or look
160	at (a `kubectl` command, or a `mise` task), in English. `Err` is kept for
161	`errors.Is`/`errors.As` and is never printed: the text of a failed sub-process can
162	carry a credential, and neither the stderr of kubectl nor its error reaches a
163	message. `ErrKind` holds the kinds of D-F in the order the bench meets them:
164	`KubectlMissing`, `ContextNotFound`, `ClusterUnreachable`, `Forbidden`,
165	`NamespaceForeign`, `NamespaceMissing`, `NodePortTaken`, `AdmissionDenied`,
166	`PodPending`, `ImagePull`, `Crash`, `Deadline`, `RESTUnreachable`,
167	`ProvisionFailed`. The zero value is `Unclassified`, so an error nobody classified
168	never passes for a named kind. `SkopeoMissing`, `RegistryUnreachable`,
169	`RegistryRefused` and `SeedFailed` (DEVDESK-505) were appended after
170	`ProvisionFailed`, so no earlier value moved (`TestSkopeoErrKindsAreAppendedAtTheEnd`).
171	
172	`classifyKubectl(stderr)` is the fallback for what the exit status and the JSON
173	cannot tell apart; kubectl's wording changes between versions, so it matches
174	lower-cased fragments and returns `Unclassified` for an unknown text. Order of the
175	rules: an admission webhook that denied (even reported as `Forbidden`) is
176	`AdmissionDenied`; `provided port is already allocated` or `... not in the valid
177	range` is `NodePortTaken`; `forbidden` is `Forbidden`; `Unable to connect to the
178	server`, `connection refused`, `i/o timeout`, `TLS handshake timeout` are
179	`ClusterUnreachable`.
180	
181	**Runner.** `Runner.Run(ctx, stdin, args...)` returns both streams even on
182	failure. `NewExecRunner(context)` finds `kubectl` with `exec.LookPath` (a
183	`KubectlMissing` error otherwise, which names `kubectl` and `mise install`) and
184	puts `--context <context>` before every call, so callers never pass it.
185	`kubectl.go` is the only non-test file of the package that starts `kubectl` (the commands of `Runner` and the port-forward, see "The two process doors" below); the other two processes are the `git check-ignore` of the secrets store (see below) and `skopeo` (`skopeo.go`).
186	
187	**Preflight.** `RunPreflight(ctx, r, p, op) (PreflightResult, error)` with `op` one
188	of `OpUp`, `OpProvision`, `OpDown`, `OpStatus`, `OpSeed` (appended, no earlier value moves). Checks, in this order, stopping at
189	the first failure:
190	
191	1. `p.Validate()`: invalid parameters are refused before any call.
192	2. `kubectl config get-contexts -o name`: the exact context name is listed, else
193	   `ContextNotFound`. Nothing else is asked.
194	3. `kubectl get --raw /readyz`: the API server answers, else `ClusterUnreachable`;
195	   a refusal (stderr `forbidden`: expired token, 403) is `Forbidden` instead, through
196	   the same `classifyKubectl` as every other call.
197	4. `kubectl auth can-i <verb> <resource> [--subresource=<sub>]` (`-n <ns>`, `-A` or
198	   nothing). A subresource is a flag, never `pods/exec` in the resource: kubectl
199	   reads that as the object `exec` of the pods and answers about the wrong thing
200	   (the NX-01 question `create pods/exec` had this defect and is corrected here:
201	   it is now `create pods --subresource=exec`). A refusal still names
202	   `pods/exec` in its cause, and its `Check` carries the flag:
203	   `up` needs create and patch `namespaces` (cluster; a server-side apply is a
204	   PATCH, also on a second run), create `persistentvolumeclaims`, `services`,
205	   `deployments` and `pods` `exec` (namespace), list `services` (`-A`),
206	   patch `deployments`, `services` and `persistentvolumeclaims`, and get and list
207	   `pods` and `persistentvolumeclaims` (the wait of `Deploy`), all in the
208	   namespace (no manifest creates a Secret, so none is asked), then, asked last
209	   so the fourteen before stay where they were, patch `deployments`
210	   `--subresource=scale` (the upstream is scaled), create `pods`
211	   `--subresource=portforward` and get `services` (the seed
212	   that follows reaches the upstream through a port-forward, which reads the
213	   Service first);
214	   `provision` needs create `pods` `exec`, get `deployments` and list `pods`
215	   (namespace); `down` needs delete `namespaces`; `seed` needs, in this order, get
216	   `deployments`, list `pods`, get `pods`, get `services`, get and list
217	   `persistentvolumeclaims` (EnsureUpstream reads the claim on every turn of its
218	   wait, so a refusal comes before the scale write), create `pods`
219	   `--subresource=portforward` and patch `deployments` `--subresource=scale`
220	   (namespace); `status` asks nothing. A `no` arrives on stdout with a non-zero exit, so stdout is read
221	   first: `Forbidden`, naming the verb and the resource.
222	5. `kubectl get namespace <ns> -o json`: absent is fine for `up` and `down` (nothing
223	   to delete) and `NamespaceMissing` for `provision`, `status` and `seed`; present
224	   without the label `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=devdesk-nexus-bench` is
225	   `NamespaceForeign` for every operation (the plan lists `up` and `down`;
226	   `provision` and `status` refuse too, so the bench never runs `exec` in a
227	   namespace it did not create).
228	6. `up` only (`seed` does not read the Services of the cluster), `kubectl get services -A -o json`: a Service other than `nexus` of
229	   our namespace that holds `HTTPNodePort` or `DockerNodePort` is `NodePortTaken`,
230	   naming `<namespace>/<name>` and the port. Our own Service is accepted, which is
231	   what makes a second `up` possible.
232	7. Everything but `down` and `seed`, `kubectl get nodes -o json` (the seed reaches
233	   the registries through a loopback port-forward and no can-i covers `get nodes`,
234	   so its `NodeIP` is empty): `NodeIP` is the first
235	   `InternalIP`; none is not an error (`NodeIP` stays empty).
236	
237	A call that fails in a way the checks above did not expect goes through
238	`classifyKubectl` (a `forbidden` stderr becomes `Forbidden`, anything unknown
239	`Unclassified`). Every call that reaches the API server carries
240	`--request-timeout=10s`.
241	
242	**No write before the end of the preflight.** The preflight issues `config`,
243	`get` and `auth can-i` only, never sends stdin, and a failure at any point leaves
244	the cluster untouched. The tests run it against a scripted fake runner that fails
245	the test on any call outside the six above and records every write verb
246	(`apply`, `create`, `delete`, `patch`, `exec`, ...) it would have seen. The
247	`Runner` of the later steps (apply, delete) is only called after `RunPreflight`
248	returned without an error.

250	## Secrets and descriptor (`secrets.go`, `descriptor.go`)
251	
252	**Secrets.** `Secrets{AdminPassword, PendingAdminPassword, PullPassword}` (JSON
253	`adminPassword`, `pendingAdminPassword`, `pullPassword`; the last two are omitted
254	when empty) is kept by a `SecretStore` (`Load`, `Save`, `Remove`), implemented by
255	`NewFileStore(path)`. `PendingAdminPassword` is the new admin password, written
256	before it is sent to Nexus, so an interrupted change loses nothing.
257	
258	- Path: `DefaultSecretsPath(context, namespace, getenv)` is
259	  `$XDG_STATE_HOME/devdesk/nexus-bench/<context>/<namespace>/secrets.json`, else
260	  `$HOME/.local/state/...` (`USERPROFILE` when `HOME` is unset); an empty variable
261	  counts as unset, none of them set is an error, and `NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS`
262	  overrides the whole path. It is outside every repository and shared by all the
263	  worktrees, so a worktree never keeps a stale admin password of its own.
264	- Modes: the file is `0600`, the folders `Save` creates are `0700`. The write is
265	  atomic (`writeFileAtomic`): a temporary file in the same folder, `chmod`, sync,
266	  rename, then a best-effort sync of the folder so the new name survives a power
267	  cut (errors ignored: Windows and some file systems cannot sync a folder); the
268	  temporary file is removed when anything fails, so a failed `Save`
269	  leaves no partial file and a file left by someone else with a wider mode is
270	  replaced, not kept. POSIX modes are not meaningful on Windows (the test skips).
271	- File name: `NewFileStore` refuses a path whose file name is not `secrets.json`
272	  (`Remove` deletes that file, and a mistyped `NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS` must not point
273	  it at `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`).
274	- Mode on read: `Load` refuses a file with a group or other bit (`mode & 0o077`),
275	  outside Windows, with a `BenchError` that never shows the content and says
276	  `chmod 600 <path>`.
277	- Display: `Secrets` has `String`, `GoString` and `LogValue` methods that all give
278	  `Secrets{redacted}`, so no fmt verb (`%v`, `%+v`, `%#v`, `%s`, `%q`) and no slog
279	  handler prints a password (`TestSecretsAreRedactedWhenFormatted`). The JSON of
280	  the file is unaffected.
281	- `Load` returns `(zero, false, nil)` when the file is absent. A file that is not a
282	  valid JSON object is a `BenchError` that names the path and never shows the
283	  content (the underlying error is kept in `Err`, which is not printed).
284	- `Remove` deletes the file, then the namespace folder when it is empty; it
285	  succeeds when there is nothing to remove, and a folder holding anything else
286	  stays.
287	- Git guard: `NewFileStore` refuses an empty path and touches nothing on disk.
288	  It walks up from the file's folder looking for a `.git` entry (directory or
289	  file, so a worktree counts); with none, the path is accepted without asking
290	  git. With one, it runs `git -C <root> check-ignore -q -- <path>`: ignored is
291	  accepted; not ignored, or git unavailable, is a `BenchError` that says to set
292	  `NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS` outside the repository. The process runs with the caller's
293	  environment minus `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`,
294	  `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_NAMESPACE`, `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`,
295	  `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_*`,
296	  `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_*`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` and
297	  `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` (`gitEnvironment`), then `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=<devnull>` and
298	  `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, so the verdict is about the repository of the path and
299	  its own ignore rules, not about a repository or a `core.excludesFile` the
300	  caller's variables or configuration point at (a path ignored only by a global
301	  excludes file is therefore refused). That call is the only process
302	  outside `kubectl.go` and `skopeo.go`; it lives in the package variable `gitIgnores`, so it can
303	  be replaced and found by a source guard.
304	
305	**Descriptor.** `BuildDescriptor(p, DeployResult, ProvisionResult, SeedResult)`
306	returns the `Descriptor` of schema 2 (D-D, D-M; schema 1 was NX-01's):
307	`schemaVersion`, `kubeContext`, `namespace`,
308	`image`, `nexusVersion`, `edition`, `eulaAccepted`, `hosts`, `rest`,
309	`dockerConnectors`, `repositories`, `realms`, `accounts`, `registryAccess`,
310	`upstream`, `dataset`, in that order, which is the
311	order of the struct fields. The three sections of schema 2 (DEVDESK-543):
312	
313	- `registryAccess`: `scheme` `http`, `tlsVerify` `false`, `routing` `path` (a
314	  client reaches the Docker repositories by path on the HTTP NodePort, plain
315	  HTTP; H-PATH is still to be proven on the bench).
316	- `upstream`: `service` `bench-upstream`, `image` `Params.UpstreamImageRef()`,
317	  `url` `Params.UpstreamURL` (the one `docker-proxy` mirrors), `persistent`
318	  `true`, `exposure` `port-forward` (the upstream has no NodePort; a client
319	  reaches it through `kubectl port-forward`).
320	- `dataset`: one entry per image of the `SeedResult`, in its order and copied
321	  (never shared): `name`, `tag`, `digest`, `location` (`docker-hosted` or
322	  `upstream`), `cachedInProxy` (= `DatasetImage.PullThrough`: Seed pulled it
323	  through `docker-proxy`). It comes from the `SeedResult`, not from `Dataset()`:
324	  an empty result writes `"dataset": []`, never `null`.
325	
326	`ProxyPending` false, the nominal case of NX-02, lists `docker-proxy` and makes
327	it a member of `docker-group`. `hosts` is `Params.Hosts` when set, else `127.0.0.1`
328	then `DeployResult.NodeIP` when it is not empty; the URLs are `http://<host>:<nodePort>`
329	for each host (`RESTBaseURL(host, p)` is the exported REST origin: brackets for
330	IPv6, `%25` for a zone; the deployment, the descriptor and the command of step 8
331	all build it there). `DeployResult{ReachableHosts, NodeIP}` (step 4) and
332	`ProvisionResult{NexusVersion, Edition, EULAAccepted}` (step 6) are defined in
333	`descriptor.go` and reused by those steps. The account `anonymous` always
334	appears; its `enabled` is a `*bool`, so `false` is written when
335	`NEXUS_BENCH_ANONYMOUS=false`, and the other accounts write no `enabled`.
336	
337	- `WriteDescriptor(path, d)`: JSON indented by two spaces, one final newline, `0644`
338	  file, atomic through the same helper; the bytes depend on `d` alone.
339	- `LoadDescriptor(path)`: a missing file is `ErrNoDescriptor` (wrapped, use
340	  `errors.Is`); invalid JSON or a `schemaVersion` other than 2 (missing counts as 0)
341	  is an error that names the file and never shows its content. A schema 1 file
342	  is a `*BenchError` (kind `Unclassified`) whose `Check` says to run `mise run
343	  nexus-bench:up` to write it again; `status` reports it as `descriptor:
344	  unreadable (...)` and still prints the pod and REST lines.
345	- `DescriptorPath()`: `NEXUS_BENCH_DESCRIPTOR` when set and not empty, else
346	  `internal/nexusbench/descriptor.json`, found with `runtime.Caller`, so it does
347	  not depend on the working directory (and does not survive `-trimpath`).
348	- Never in the descriptor: a password or any secret, the path of the secrets file,
349	  a timestamp, a pod name, or the word `password` (`TestDescriptorHoldsNoSecret`,
350	  `TestDescriptorFormat`).
351	
352	The golden `testdata/descriptor.example.json` is the descriptor of `Defaults()`
353	with node IP `192.168.1.31`, Nexus `3.98.1-01`, `COMMUNITY`, EULA accepted. It is
354	checked both ways: `WriteDescriptor` must write exactly these bytes
355	(`TestDescriptorGolden`) and `LoadDescriptor` must read back `BuildDescriptor`'s
356	value (`TestLoadDescriptorGoldenMatchesBuild`). After a deliberate change of the
357	schema, regenerate it with
358	`go test ./internal/nexusbench -run TestDescriptorGolden -update` and review the
359	diff by hand (bump `schemaVersion` when a field changes meaning). The golden holds
360	the whole `Dataset()` (`SeedResult{Images: Dataset()}`), with `mirror/cached` as the
361	only image cached in the proxy.

363	## REST client and provisioning (`nexusapi.go`, `provision.go`, `initialpassword.go`)
364	
365	`Provision(ctx, baseURL, ip, store, p, out) (ProvisionResult, error)` brings a
366	running Nexus to the state the bench needs (D-E). `baseURL` is the REST origin
367	(no path); `ip` is an `InitialPassword` (`Read(ctx) (pw, ok, err)`); `out` gets
368	progress lines (`provision: ...`) and never a password.
369	
370	**Idempotence.** Every object is read, then created when absent or replaced when
371	present; there is no "create and ignore the error". A second run sends no `POST`
372	(except the one `POST` of a proxy whose upstream does not resolve yet, see
373	"Unresolvable upstream" under call 9 below) and changes neither the state nor
374	any password. Order of the calls:
375	
376	1. `GET /v1/status` (no account): version and edition from the `Server` header
377	   (`Nexus/3.98.1-01 (COMMUNITY)`), else `info.version` of
378	   `/service/rest/swagger.json`, else empty (a note on `out`). The version is
379	   optional: a swagger answer that is a refusal or not JSON (a proxy page) leaves
380	   it empty; only a transport failure stops the run.
381	2. Admin credentials (below).
382	3. EULA: `GET /v1/system/eula`; 404 means an edition without one (noted,
383	   `EULAAccepted` false); `accepted: true` changes nothing; otherwise it is
384	   accepted only when `Params.AcceptEULA` (`NEXUS_BENCH_ACCEPT_EULA=yes`), with
385	   `POST {"accepted":true,"disclaimer":<as received>}`; the disclaimer is kept as
386	   a `json.RawMessage`, never rebuilt. Without consent `Provision` stops with a
387	   `ProvisionFailed` that names `NEXUS_BENCH_ACCEPT_EULA` and says that no
388	   repository, role or account was created, before any creation (the
389	   only write before it is the admin password change, which the EULA read needs).
390	4. Blob store: `GET /v1/blobstores` must list `default`, else `ProvisionFailed`
391	   before any role, user or repository is created.
392	5. Realms: `GET /v1/security/realms/active`; the missing ones of
393	   `NexusAuthenticatingRealm`, `DockerToken` are appended and the list is
394	   `PUT` back (a list that is already complete is not written). The plan said
395	   "set these two"; appending keeps a realm the instance already needs.
396	6. Anonymous access: `GET`, then always `PUT {"enabled": Params.Anonymous,
397	   "userId": "anonymous", "realmName": <current, default NexusAuthorizingRealm>}`.
398	7. Role `bench-docker-pull` (`nx-repository-view-docker-*-browse` and `-read`):
399	   `GET` 404 then `POST`, found then `PUT`.
400	8. User `bench-pull` (role above, status `active`): `GET /users?userId=bench-pull`,
401	   then `POST` with the password, or `PUT` plus `PUT .../change-password` with the
402	   stored password. The list filter matches by substring, so the element whose
403	   `userId` is exactly `bench-pull` is the one used.
404	9. `docker-hosted`, `docker-proxy` (`remoteUrl` = `Params.UpstreamURL`,
405	   `indexType: REGISTRY`) and `docker-group` (members hosted then proxy,
406	   `docker.httpPort: 8082`), all on blob store `default`, `forceBasicAuth: false`
407	   (anonymous pulls): `GET .../{name}` 404 then `POST`, found then `PUT`.
408	   **Unresolvable upstream.** Nexus resolves the host of the proxy's remote URL
409	   when it saves the repository and answers `400` (validation error on
410	   `proxy.remoteUrl`) when it does not. The client keeps one verdict from that
411	   answer, `APIError.RemoteURLBlocked` (a boolean, true only for a `400` with an
412	   entry whose id ends in `proxy.remoteUrl` and whose message contains `resolve
413	   host`, case-insensitive, in a body of at most 4 KiB; the body is parsed and
414	   dropped, no text of it is kept or printed; a malformed URL or any other
415	   refusal of that field is an ordinary failure). On that verdict `Provision`
416	   writes `provision: warning: Nexus refused the remote URL of docker-proxy: it
417	   cannot resolve the upstream host yet, so it was left out; run up again once
418	   the upstream exists`, goes on, creates the group with `docker-hosted` as its only
419	   member, and returns `ProvisionResult.ProxyPending` (true only when the proxy
420	   does not exist; an existing proxy stays, stays a member, and the warning says
421	   `left as it was`). Any other `400`, or a `400` on another repository, still
422	   fails. `BuildDescriptor` then lists neither `docker-proxy` nor it as a group
423	   member. A run after NX-02 deployed the upstream creates the proxy and updates
424	   the group, and the descriptor changes (commit it). So a second `up` is not
425	   POST-free while the proxy is pending: it sends the one refused `POST` of the
426	   proxy.
427	
428	**Admin credentials, a state machine with the write first.** `Load` the store;
429	the candidates are `adminPassword`, then `pendingAdminPassword`; an empty value
430	is never tried (a `{}` file means "not provided", and no request carries an empty
431	password). A candidate is accepted when `GET /v1/security/users?userId=admin`
432	answers 2xx; a 401 is a refusal and goes to the next candidate, any other status
433	is an error (a redirect or a 500 is not "wrong password"). A pending password
434	that the instance accepts is promoted to `adminPassword` with no new change.
435	When no candidate works, `InitialPassword.Read` supplies the password of the pod:
436	absent or refused gives the error `the bench admin password is unknown ...`, with
437	the check `mise run nexus-bench:down`, then `up`. Otherwise a password is
438	generated (or the stored pending one is reused), **`Save` stores it as
439	`pendingAdminPassword` first**, then `PUT /users/admin/change-password`
440	(`text/plain`) runs with the initial password, then `Save` promotes it to
441	`adminPassword`. A failed `Save` stops the run before the instance is touched
442	(`TestProvisionStopsWhenSaveFails`); a crash between the steps is resumed from the
443	pending password on the next run. The pull password follows the same rule: stored
444	before the user is created or its password set.
445	
446	**Generated passwords** are 32 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9]` from `crypto/rand`
447	(rejection sampling, no modulo bias), never a fixed or predictable value.
448	
449	**`kubectlInitialPassword`** (`NewKubectlInitialPassword(runner, namespace)`) runs
450	`-n <ns> exec deploy/nexus -- cat /nexus-data/admin.password` through the
451	`Runner`, so `kubectl.go` stays the only file that starts a process. A "No such
452	file or directory" on stderr is (empty, false, nil); another failure is a
453	`BenchError` (kind from `classifyKubectl`, else `ProvisionFailed`) whose message
454	holds neither stdout nor stderr. Unit-tested on a fake `Runner`; no integration
455	test.
456	
457	**Client** (`client`, `newClient(baseURL, user, password)`): a dedicated
458	`http.Client` with `Timeout` 15 s, no proxy (the environment's proxy would receive
459	the credentials), and a `CheckRedirect` that returns `http.ErrUseLastResponse`:
460	no redirection is followed, so the 3xx is the answer and the target is never
461	contacted or named. A 2xx answer is read through `io.LimitReader` at 1 MiB + 1;
462	more is a `tooLargeError` and the content is never decoded (exactly 1 MiB is
463	read). Basic auth is set per request, only when there is a user; no header is
464	logged.
465	
466	**Errors.** `*APIError{Op, Status}` prints `<Op>: HTTP <status> <text>`: no URL,
467	no request or answer body. `Provision` returns `*BenchError` only:
468	`RESTUnreachable` when a call got no answer, `ProvisionFailed` otherwise, with
469	the `*APIError` (or the store or pod error) in `Err` so `errors.As` and
470	`errors.Is` reach it. A 401 or 403 adds the hint that the stored admin password
471	may not match. No error and no line on `out` holds a password
472	(`TestProvisionNeverPrintsAPassword`, and `requireQuiet` after every scenario,
473	which knows every password the fake saw).
474	
475	**H-REST: unverified hypotheses.** The in-memory Nexus of `fakenexus_test.go`
476	(`httptest`, loopback) is the one place that knows the JSON shapes, and it was
477	written from the Sonatype documentation, not from an instance. To check against
478	`/service/rest/swagger.json` at step 10, and to fix in the fake and the client
479	together:
480	
481	- the `Server` header on `/v1/status`, and the swagger fallback;
482	- the EULA payload and the `404` of an edition without one;
483	- `change-password` as `text/plain`, and whether `admin.password` is deleted once
484	  the password is changed through the API;
485	- the realm ids (`DockerToken`) and that the active list can be read and `PUT`;
486	- the anonymous payload (`enabled`, `userId`, `realmName`);
487	- the role and user payloads (`source` only on `PUT`, `externalRoles`), and a
488	  `userId` filter that matches by substring;
489	- the repository payloads (`storage`, `docker`, `proxy`, `dockerProxy`,
490	  `negativeCache`, `httpClient`, `group.memberNames`, `docker.httpPort`), the
491	  statuses of `POST` (201) and `PUT` (204), the path-routing field added in 3.83
492	  (left to the default of Nexus), and a proxy created before its upstream exists.
493	
494	Verdict of the first real run (details in "First real run"): every item above
495	held except the last one. The `Server` header, the EULA payload, `text/plain`
496	change-password, the realm ids, the anonymous, role, user and repository
497	payloads and all the statuses matched the swagger and the fake. A proxy created
498	before its upstream resolves is refused with `400`; the fake does the same since
499	(`BlockUpstream`, `ResolveUpstream`).
500	
501	**Reading a stored bench: `adminFromStore`, `listComponents` (`components.go`,
502	DEVDESK-541, NX-02a).** For the commands that run after `up` (seed, restore,
503	reset).
504	
505	- `adminFromStore(ctx, baseURL, store)` returns a `*client` that authenticates as
506	  `admin` with the stored `AdminPassword`, and the stored `Secrets` (so the caller
507	  has the `bench-pull` password too). It sends no request: a stored password the
508	  instance refuses shows on the first call as an `*APIError` 401. It never reads
509	  the initial password of the pod and never falls back to it. No stored admin
510	  password (no file, `{}`, only a pending or a pull password: a pending password
511	  is not a current one) is a `*BenchError` of kind `ProvisionFailed` whose `Check`
512	  says to run `mise run nexus-bench:up`; so is a store that cannot be read, with
513	  the cause in `Err` and not in the message.
514	- `(*client).listComponents(ctx, repo)` calls `GET /v1/components?repository=<repo>`
515	  and follows `continuationToken` (sent through `url.Values`, so escaped) until it
516	  is `null`. A `404` (a repository that does not exist, was just deleted, or is a
517	  proxy still pending) is an empty list, not an error; a `404` on a later page is
518	  an `*APIError`. Failures are those of the rest of the client: `*APIError`
519	  (`list the components of <repo>`), `*transportError`, `*tooLargeError`,
520	  `*decodeError`; an error on any page returns no component at all, never the
521	  first pages. A token equal to the previous one fails at once with a
522	  `*decodeError` (no `APIError`, no `BenchError`); a listing whose tokens keep
523	  changing stops after 1000 calls with the same error. A `component` is `{Name, Version, Digest}`; `Digest` is
524	  `sha256:` + the checksum of the asset whose path holds `/manifests/` (the one
525	  ending in the tag first), and is empty, without an error, when the instance
526	  lists no such asset. No delete and no unblock here (NX-02b).
527	- **H-COMPONENTS: unverified.** A Docker component is one image tag (`name` the
528	  image name, `version` the tag), the manifest asset is `v2/<name>/manifests/<tag>`
529	  and its `sha256` checksum is the digest of the manifest; the blob assets come
530	  first in the list. Written from the Sonatype documentation and the fake; to
531	  check against a real listing at step 12 (name of a nested image, a manifest list
532	  versus a single manifest, whether the checksum is the digest the registry
533	  serves) and to fix in the fake and the client together.
534	
535	**Security guarantees.** No redirect followed; answers bounded; no proxy; no
536	`Authorization` header, URL with credentials, body or password in any error or
537	output; passwords written to the store before use; an empty password never sent;
538	no process started outside `kubectl.go`.
539	
540	## Destruction and the clock (`destroy.go`, `clock.go`)
541	
542	`Destroy(ctx, runner, clock, store, params, out)` is the one irreversible
543	operation of the bench (risk R1), so its order is fixed:
544	
545	1. `RunPreflight(OpDown)`: `Validate` first (no call at all), then context,
546	   `/readyz`, `auth can-i delete namespaces`, and the namespace. A namespace
547	   without the label `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=devdesk-nexus-bench` is
548	   refused here with `NamespaceForeign`, before any write.
549	2. A namespace that is absent prints `nothing to delete` and succeeds. The
550	   stored secrets are removed anyway, so a stale `secrets.json` does not
551	   outlive its bench and a second `down` is idempotent.
552	3. **One write**: `delete namespace <ns> --wait=false`, issued once, never
553	   retried (a `Forbidden` is returned as is). Nothing else is ever written: no
554	   finalizer patch, no force delete, no delete of another object. The tests
555	   journal every call and fail on a second write.
556	4. The namespace is read (`get namespace <ns> -o json`) until `NotFound` or
557	   `NEXUS_BENCH_DELETE_TIMEOUT` (default 3 min). The first read is immediate; the
558	   interval between reads doubles from 1 s to 10 s, always through `Clock.Sleep`
559	   and clipped to what remains of the timeout. A namespace stuck in `Terminating`
560	   ends in a `Deadline` error that cites the namespace, `spec.finalizers` and
561	   each `status.conditions` entry (type, status, message); the bench does not
562	   remove them.
563	5. One read of `get pv -o json`. A PersistentVolume whose `claimRef.namespace` is
564	   the bench namespace prints a line starting with `warning:` that names it and
565	   its phase and says it still exists: the run still succeeds, because the
566	   reclaim policy decides (`Delete` may remove it seconds later, `Retain` keeps
567	   the data on the node) and the bench does not delete a volume itself. No such volume, no
568	   warning. A PV list that cannot be read is also a warning, not a failure.
569	6. `store.Remove()`, last, and only when the namespace is gone. Its failure is
570	   returned as a `BenchError` (the namespace is already deleted; running `down`
571	   again retries the removal). A failed or cancelled run never touches the
572	   secrets.
573	
574	A cancelled context ends the wait with an error that wraps `context.Canceled`
575	(`errors.Is` holds); the namespace keeps terminating on the cluster. Lines on
576	`out` start with `down:` and, like every error, hold no password.
577	
578	`Clock` (`Now`, `Sleep(ctx, d) error`) is how the waits spend time. `NewClock()`
579	is the wall clock: `Sleep` returns `ctx.Err()` when the context is done (before
580	sleeping, even for a zero duration), returns at once for `d <= 0`, and otherwise
581	waits on a timer or the context. `fakeClock` of `clock_test.go` moves its time
582	forward instead of waiting, so no test sleeps for real.
583	
584	## Deployment and the wait (`deploy.go`, `probe.go`)
585	
586	`Deploy(ctx, runner, prober, clock, params, out) (DeployResult, error)` applies
587	the manifests and waits until Nexus answers. Order, fixed:
588	
589	1. `RunPreflight(OpUp)`, whole; no write before it succeeds.
590	2. `ctx` is looked at (a runner may ignore it), then
591	   `kubectl apply --server-side --field-manager=devdesk-nexus-bench -f -` with
592	   `RenderNamespace(p)` on stdin: the Namespace alone, so a failure later leaves
593	   at worst our labeled namespace and never anything outside it.
594	3. The same apply with `Render(p)`: the whole stream, the Namespace again
595	   included. A second `up` sends the same two applies and gets the same result;
596	   `--prune` is never used.
597	4. The wait, one round per `pollInterval` (5 s) through `Clock.Sleep`: read
598	   `get pods -n <ns> -l app.kubernetes.io/name=nexus -o json` and
599	   `get pvc -n <ns> -o json` (the list; the claim of Nexus, `nexus-data`, is
600	   picked by name), diagnose them, then probe every host. The deadline
601	   is `NEXUS_BENCH_TIMEOUT` (10 min); it is checked after a round, so the cluster
602	   is read once more at the very end.
603	
604	**Failure of an apply** is classified from its stderr by `classifyKubectl`:
605	`NodePortTaken` (names `NEXUS_BENCH_HTTP_NODEPORT` and `..._DOCKER_NODEPORT`),
606	`AdmissionDenied` (a webhook refusal wins over the `Forbidden` the API server
607	also reports), `Forbidden`, `ClusterUnreachable`, else `Unclassified`. The
608	runner's error is the `Err` of the `BenchError` (for `errors.Is`); neither the
609	stderr nor the error of the prober is ever in a message. After a failed apply
610	nothing else is called: no read, no probe, no sleep.
611	
612	**Diagnosis**, each round, on the pods that are not being deleted:
613	
614	| Reading | Kind | When |
615	|---|---|---|
616	| container waiting on `ErrImagePull` or `ImagePullBackOff` | `ImagePull` (names the image and `NEXUS_BENCH_IMAGE`, `_IMAGE_TAG`) | at once |
617	| `CrashLoopBackOff`, or `OOMKilled` as last or current termination | `Crash` (names the memory limit and `NEXUS_BENCH_MEMORY_LIMIT`) | at once |
618	| `PodScheduled=False`, reason `Unschedulable`, message with `Insufficient memory` or `Insufficient cpu` | `PodPending` (the request and `NEXUS_BENCH_MEMORY_REQUEST` or `_CPU_REQUEST`) | after `pendingGrace` (30 s) |
619	| claim `Pending` while a pod is scheduled | `PodPending` (the size and `NEXUS_BENCH_STORAGE_SIZE`) | after `pendingGrace` |
620	| no host answers by the deadline | `Deadline` (last state of the pod and the claim, the hosts tried, `NEXUS_BENCH_TIMEOUT`) | at `Params.Timeout` |
621	
622	**One diagnosis, two workloads (DEVDESK-540).** The wait and the table above take a
623	`workload` (`deploy.go`): the pod selector, the variables that set the image and
624	the memory, the name of the claim and of the Deployment, and how to name them in a
625	message. `nexusWorkload()` is Nexus; `upstreamWorkload()` is the pod of the bench
626	upstream, whose memory is fixed by its manifest (no memory variable, so `Crash`
627	says `the bench-upstream container keeps crashing` without a limit nor a variable
628	to raise, `PodPending` for a lack of memory or cpu names no request, the pending
629	claim names no `NEXUS_BENCH_STORAGE_SIZE`, and `ImagePull` names
630	`NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_IMAGE` and `_IMAGE_TAG` and the upstream reference). The claim
631	is selected by name in the list `get pvc -n <ns> -o json`: the namespace holds the
632	claims of Nexus and of the upstream, kubectl lists them by name, and reading
633	`Items[0]` read the claim of the upstream (`bench-upstream-data`) instead of
634	`nexus-data` once the upstream manifests were applied, so a Pending claim of the
635	upstream was blamed on Nexus (`TestDeployReadsTheClaimOfNexusOnly`).
636	
637	The unschedulable pod is read before the claim: while the pod is not scheduled, a
638	claim of a `WaitForFirstConsumer` class is `Pending` for that reason alone and is
639	not blamed. A reading that changes or disappears restarts the grace count (the
640	volume binds when the pod is scheduled; the Deployment may have made no pod yet).
641	When the deadline arrives with such a reading still active, it is returned as
642	`PodPending` rather than `Deadline`. A cancelled context is returned as is
643	(`errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)`), never as a `Deadline`.
644	
645	**Reached hosts.** The hosts are `Params.Hosts` when set, else `127.0.0.1` and
646	the node `InternalIP` (when there is one). Each round probes them in parallel at
647	`http://<host>:<HTTPNodePort>` (`net.JoinHostPort`, so IPv6 gets brackets) and
648	returns after the first round in which at least one answered, with
649	`DeployResult.ReachableHosts` = the hosts that answered in that round, in host
650	order. A host that did not answer then gets a line on `out` that starts with
651	`deploy: warning:` and names it; no warning when all answered. `BuildDescriptor`
652	lists in `hosts` (and in every URL) `Params.Hosts` when set, else
653	`ReachableHosts` when not empty, else the earlier fallback (`127.0.0.1` and
654	`NodeIP`), so the descriptor never promises a host that did not answer
655	(`descriptor_hosts_test.go`).
656	
657	**Prober** (`probe.go`): `NewProber()` is one unauthenticated `GET
658	<baseURL>/service/rest/v1/status` on a dedicated client (5 s timeout, no proxy,
659	no keep-alive, `CheckRedirect` returning `http.ErrUseLastResponse`): nil on 200
660	and only then, otherwise a `*APIError` (status only) or a `*transportError`
661	(wrapping the cause for `errors.Is`). The body is neither read for its content
662	nor reported, and a redirect target is never contacted.
663	
664	**Rights the deployment needs** (all asked by the preflight, namespace-scoped
665	except the first two): create and patch `namespaces` (cluster); create and patch
666	`persistentvolumeclaims`, `services`, `deployments`; get and list `pods` and
667	`persistentvolumeclaims`; create `pods/exec` (used by `Provision`); list `services` in all namespaces (NodePort check).
668	
669	**Not covered by the fakes.** `Deploy` has only run against a scripted `Runner`,
670	a fake `Prober` and a fake `Clock`; the real kubectl output shape of
671	`get pods -o json` (container status fields), the real duration of the pull and
672	the start, and whether `kubectl apply --server-side` of a Namespace that carries
673	no field of its own conflicts on a second run were left for step 10: the real
674	output was read, a second `up` applied the same two documents with no conflict,
675	and the start took 48 s (see "First real run").
676	
677	## Residual risks (security audit of the steps 4, 6, 7)
678	
679	Known and accepted for a throw-away bench; none is fixed by this change.
680	
681	- **Basic credentials in clear HTTP.** Nexus is reached on `http://`, so the admin
682	  and `bench-pull` credentials of `Provision` travel unencrypted. The command
683	  honours the commitment made for it: it sends them to
684	  `RESTBaseURL("127.0.0.1", p)` and to another host only on `--rest-host`, with a
685	  warning (see "The command"). The package itself does not enforce it.
686	- **`local-path` volume in `0777`.** The data folder of the local-path
687	  provisioner is world-writable, so `admin.password` is readable by every local
688	  account of the node between the start of Nexus and the provisioning (which
689	  changes it).
690	- **NodePorts on the LAN, anonymous access on purpose.** The two NodePorts listen
691	  on every interface of the node, and anonymous access is enabled by default so
692	  that pulls need no login (`NEXUS_BENCH_ANONYMOUS`). Anyone on the LAN can read
693	  the bench; do not put anything private in it.
694	- **Mutable image tag.** The image is `docker.io/sonatype/nexus3:<tag>` with no
695	  digest: the same tag can resolve to another image later.
696	- **Partial result on error.** `Provision` returns the `ProvisionResult` it had
697	  gathered together with the error. The command does not write the descriptor
698	  when `err != nil` (`TestDescriptorIsNotWrittenUnlessProvisionSucceeded`), or it
699	  would describe a bench that is half provisioned.
700	
701	## The command and the mise tasks (`cmd/nexus-bench`, `mise.toml`)
702	
703	`internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench` is a `package main` of five files:
704	`main.go` (`deps`, `defaultDeps`, `run`), `flags.go` (flags and parameter
705	resolution), `commands.go` (`up`, `provision`, `down`, `seed`, `render`), `status.go` and
706	`usage.go` (the help). `main()` only builds a context cancelled by SIGINT and
707	SIGTERM, calls `run(ctx, args, os.Getenv, os.Stdout, os.Stderr, defaultDeps())`
708	and exits with its code. `deps` holds every constructor and library call that
709	reaches a cluster (`newRunner`, `newProber`, `clock`, `newStore`, `newInitial`,
710	`preflight`, `deploy`, `provision`, `destroy`) and, since NX-02a (DEVDESK-544),
711	the doors of the seed and the reads of `status` (`newForwarder`, `newCopier`,
712	`ensureUpstream`, `seed`, `readUpstream`, `readImages`); `defaultDeps` wires
713	`NewExecRunner`, `NewProber`, `NewClock`, `NewFileStore`,
714	`NewKubectlInitialPassword`, `RunPreflight`, `Deploy`, `Provision`, `Destroy`,
715	`NewExecPortForwarder`, `NewSkopeoCopier`, `EnsureUpstream`, `Seed`,
716	`ReadUpstream` and `readImagesAnonymously` (which calls `ListImagesAnonymously`),
717	and the tests wire fakes, so no test needs kubectl, skopeo or a network.
718	
719	**Tasks.** Seven, in `mise.toml`, none reachable from `ci`, `check`, `test` or
720	`test-race` (`mise_tasks_test.go` reads the file and checks it, and checks that
721	`kubectl` is declared on each of them, not in the global `[tools]`, so the CI does
722	not install it; kubectl `1.35`, because `datomir` runs k0s v1.36.x and kubectl is
723	supported within one minor version of the API server, so 1.35 is the oldest
724	accepted; `render` contacts no cluster and declares no kubectl, and the test
725	requires its absence there). `nexus-bench:seed` needs `skopeo` too, which is a
726	tool of the host: mise does not install it, the task does not declare it, and its
727	description says so (`TestMiseSeedTaskNamesSkopeoAsAPrerequisiteOfTheHost`).
728	Arguments follow `--`: mise appends them to the command line.
729	
730	| Task | Runs | Acts on the cluster |
731	|---|---|---|
732	| `nexus-bench:up` | `go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench up` | yes |
733	| `nexus-bench:provision` | `... provision` | yes (REST and `exec`) |
734	| `nexus-bench:down` | `... down` | yes (deletes the namespace) |
735	| `nexus-bench:seed` | `... seed` | yes (port-forward, REST reads, skopeo pushes); needs skopeo on the host |
736	| `nexus-bench:status` | `... status` | reads only |
737	| `nexus-bench:render` | `... render` | no, contacts nothing |
738	| `nexus-bench:test` | `go test -timeout 60m -count=1 -run Integration ./internal/nexusbench/...` with `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH=1` set by the task's `env` table (portable, no `env` command) | yes; the tests skip when `CI` is set |
739	
740	**Subcommands and flags.** Every subcommand takes the same parameter flags, one
741	per `NEXUS_BENCH_*` variable: `--context`, `--namespace`, `--http-nodeport`,
742	`--docker-nodeport`, `--cpu-request`, `--cpu-limit`, `--memory-request`,
743	`--memory-limit`, `--storage-size`, `--jvm-opts`, `--image`, `--image-tag`,
744	`--upstream-image`, `--upstream-image-tag`, `--upstream-url`, `--anonymous`,
745	`--hosts`, `--timeout`, `--delete-timeout`, `--secrets`, `--descriptor`. `up`
746	and `provision` add `--accept-eula` and `--rest-host`; `seed` adds `--rest-host`
747	only (it provisions nothing, so there is no EULA to accept). Each subcommand has its own `flag.FlagSet` (`ContinueOnError`,
748	output discarded: the command prints parse errors itself on stderr and `-h` on
749	stdout). A flag is laid over its variable and the result goes through
750	`FromEnv(Defaults(), ...)` once, so "flag, then `NEXUS_BENCH_*`, then default",
751	the parsing and the rule that `--namespace` moves the upstream URL (unless an
752	upstream is given, by flag or variable) are the library's own. `--accept-eula`
753	becomes `yes` (and `--accept-eula=false` `no`, which beats a variable set to
754	`yes`). `Validate` runs before anything else, `render` included.
755	
756	**Exit codes.** `0` success; `1` failure (invalid parameter, kubectl missing, a
757	step failed, a run cancelled); `2` mistake in the command line (no or unknown
758	subcommand, unknown flag, a value of the wrong type, a missing value, an extra
759	argument), with the help on stderr when the subcommand is missing or unknown.
760	`help`, `-h` and `--help` print on stdout and exit `0`. `go run` (so every
761	`mise run nexus-bench:*`) does not propagate the code: it prints `exit status 2`
762	and exits `1`. Code `2` is only visible when the compiled binary is run directly;
763	the general help says so (`TestHelpSaysGoRunDoesNotKeepExitCodeTwo`).
764	
765	**Interruption.** `main()` cancels the run's context on SIGINT or SIGTERM and
766	then hands the signals back to the default behavior (`context.AfterFunc(ctx,
767	stop)`), so a second Ctrl-C kills a run that is slow to wind down. This is not
768	unit-tested: it lives in `main()`, which the tests do not call.
769	
770	**Output.** The progress of the library steps goes to stdout, then one line
771	`nexus-bench: descriptor written to <path>`. Every failure is one line on stderr:
772	a `BenchError` (also when wrapped by `%w` or joined) prints exactly its
773	`Error()`, and nothing around it or inside it (no wrapper text, no `Err`, no
774	trace); a cancelled run says `cancelled` and that `status` shows where things

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)

    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one animation tick (blink phase, `app.motion`), the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`, `ChangedMsg.Failures`), the activity-column guard (`activity_guard_test.go`), the tab progress bar (OSC 9;4, `terminalProgress`), the window title (`windowTitle`, restored by `internal/termtitle`), the terminal hand-off to child processes (the exec wrapper `internal/ui/teaexec`, use it instead of `tea.ExecProcess`, D121) and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci` (typed `StatusError`, `...Context` variants), `internal/imagesearch` and the registry browser's image search level, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface`, `internal/nettrace` (the path trace: unprivileged UDP + `IP_RECVERR` on Linux, ICMP echo through `iphlpapi` on native Windows) |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage`, `internal/ui/datatable`, and the activity indicator column (`internal/ui/indicator`, `datatable.IndicatorColumn`, the row sentences `components.DescribeRow`) |
| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |
| [`nexus-bench.md`](../docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md) | `internal/nexusbench` — the disposable Nexus Community bench on the k0s cluster (DEVDESK-504, NX-01): decisions, the `NEXUS_BENCH_*` parameters and their validation, manifests, preflight, deployment, provisioning, destruction, the `nexus-bench` command (`cmd/nexus-bench`) and its `mise run nexus-bench:*` tasks, what is still to come; a development tool outside `mise run ci` |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.
