1128	## The two process doors: port-forward and skopeo (`kubectl.go`, `skopeo.go`, DEVDESK-539)
1129	
1130	NX-02 needs two more processes: a `kubectl port-forward` to reach the upstream
1131	registry Service from this machine, and `skopeo` to push the data set into it and
1132	into the bench Nexus. Both are started from one file each, and both are written so
1133	that a failure leaves no process and no secret behind.
1134	
1135	**Port-forward.** `PortForwarder.Forward(ctx, namespace, service, port)` runs
1136	`kubectl --context <c> -n <ns> port-forward svc/<service> :<port> --address
1137	127.0.0.1` (`NewExecPortForwarder`, `KubectlMissing` like `NewExecRunner`; the
1138	namespace and the Service name are checked against a DNS-like pattern first) and
1139	returns `127.0.0.1:<port>`, the port kubectl chose, with a `stop` function.
1140	
1141	- The address comes from `parseForwardingLine`, which accepts only
1142	  `Forwarding from 127.0.0.1:<port> -> ...` with a port from 1 to 65535; the IPv6
1143	  line kubectl prints as well, another address, and `127.0.0.1.evil.com` are
1144	  ignored. The wait is `portForwardTimeout` (15 s, a variable so a test can shorten
1145	  it); a `Deadline` `BenchError` after it.
1146	- One goroutine calls `cmd.Wait`, so kubectl is always reaped, whoever ended it.
1147	  `stop` kills the process and waits for that goroutine, any number of times
1148	  (`sync.Once`), and always returns nil. The cancellation of `ctx` kills kubectl
1149	  too (`exec.CommandContext`), whether `Forward` is still waiting (it kills, waits
1150	  and returns an error) or has returned. After every error path the process is
1151	  gone.
1152	- kubectl exiting before the line is a `BenchError` whose kind comes from
1153	  `classifyKubectl(stderr)`; the stderr (capped at 16 KiB) picks the kind and is
1154	  never put in a message.
1155	
1156	**skopeo.** `ImageCopier` has two methods, `Copy(ctx, src, dst, CopyOptions)` and
1157	`ManifestDigest(ctx, ref, creds)`; `ImageRef{Transport, Location}` is `oci`, `dir` or
1158	`docker` (the location of a docker reference has no `//`). `NewSkopeoCopier` finds
1159	skopeo on PATH (`SkopeoMissing`).
1160	
1161	- *Loopback only.* TLS verification is switched off (`--src-tls-verify=false`,
1162	  `--dest-tls-verify=false`, `--tls-verify=false`) for every docker reference and
1163	  for no other, so the host is the only protection: `checkSide` refuses, **before
1164	  anything is created or started**, a docker reference whose host is not one of
1165	  the two literals `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]` (an optional port), or that has no `/`
1166	  followed by a repository name: without one skopeo reads `localhost:5000` as an
1167	  image of docker.io, with TLS off. `localhost` is not accepted, it resolves
1168	  through the host's configuration. The host is the text before the first `/`,
1169	  parsed with `net.SplitHostPort` (never a prefix test), so `127.0.0.1@evil.com`,
1170	  `127.0.0.1.evil.com`, `127.0.0.1:5000@evil.com`, `localhost`, `localhost.evil.com`
1171	  and `evil.com/127.0.0.1:5000/x` are refused, as are a LAN address (the node
1172	  itself), an empty host and `127.0.0.1:5000/`. An unknown transport, and
1173	  credentials given for an `oci` or `dir` side, are refused the same way. The
1174	  `oci` and `dir` locations are paths and are not read as hosts.
1175	- *Credentials.* A side with no credentials gets `--src-no-creds` /
1176	  `--dest-no-creds` / `--no-creds`; a side with credentials gets `--*authfile
1177	  <file>`, a container auth file `{"auths":{"<host[:port]>":{"auth":"<base64
1178	  user:password>"}}}`. There is one file per side, so the credentials of one are
1179	  never offered to the other. No password is ever an argument (visible through
1180	  `/proc`) or an environment variable. `Credentials` implements `fmt.Formatter`
1181	  (every verb, `%d` and `%x` included, prints `Credentials{User: <redacted>,
1182	  Password: REDACTED`), `String`, `GoString` and `slog.LogValuer`, and the
1183	  password has `json:"-"`.
1184	- *Working folder.* Each call makes `os.MkdirTemp` (`0700`), writes in it
1185	  `policy.json` (`{"default":[{"type":"insecureAcceptAnything"}]}`, given with
1186	  `--policy` before the subcommand; `--insecure-policy` is never used), an empty
1187	  `registries.conf` and the authentication files (`0600`), and `defer`s
1188	  `os.RemoveAll`. The folder is gone after a success, a skopeo failure and a
1189	  cancellation (the tests point `TMPDIR` at a folder and require it empty).
1190	- *Environment* (`skopeoEnvironment(registriesConf)`, modelled on
1191	  `gitEnvironment`): the caller's, without `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`,
1192	  `ALL_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` (any case), `REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE` and every `CONTAINERS_*`
1193	  variable, then `CONTAINERS_REGISTRIES_CONF=<the empty file>`, so no proxy,
1194	  mirror, login or policy of the host applies. Names are compared in upper case
1195	  (Windows). `HOME` and `PATH` are kept.
1196	- *Digest.* `ManifestDigest` runs `skopeo inspect --raw` (stdout capped at 4 MiB)
1197	  and computes the sha256 in Go, so the answer does not depend on anything skopeo
1198	  says about the manifest. `Copy` takes `--preserve-digests` from the options.
1199	- *Errors.* Always a `*BenchError`. The stderr of skopeo (capped at 64 KiB) only
1200	  picks the kind through `classifySkopeo` and is never in a message, nor is its
1201	  stdout; `Err` is the exit status of the process. A cancelled or expired context
1202	  is `Unclassified` or `Deadline`. `classifySkopeo` matches lower-cased fragments:
1203	  `connection refused`, `no such host`, `i/o timeout` give `RegistryUnreachable`;
1204	  `unauthorized`, `denied:` and `requested access to the resource is denied`
1205	  (a bare `permission denied` of a local folder is `Unclassified`),
1206	  `authentication required` (what skopeo 1.18.0 says to
1207	  a push without a login, found by the real-skopeo test) and a whole-word `403`
1208	  (a port like 40399 does not count) give `RegistryRefused`; `manifest unknown`
1209	  gives `SeedFailed`; anything else `Unclassified`.
1210	
1211	**Accepted risks of the two doors** (audit of DEVDESK-539, single-user development
1212	machine):
1213	
1214	- The loopback guard checks the host of the registry reference only. It does not
1215	  check the `realm` of a Bearer challenge a registry sends back, so a registry
1216	  could point skopeo at another host to fetch a token; the registries the bench
1217	  talks to are the bench's own (the upstream through the port-forward, the bench
1218	  Nexus), which do not do it.
1219	- A SIGKILL of the Go process skips the `defer`s and the context kill: a
1220	  `kubectl port-forward` can outlive it, and the temporary folder
1221	  (`/tmp/devdesk-skopeo-*`, `0700`, with an authentication file `0600` holding the
1222	  admin password while a call ran) can stay on disk. Nothing sweeps them; remove
1223	  them by hand.
1224	- While a port-forward lives, its `127.0.0.1:<port>` is reachable by every local
1225	  account, without credentials of the upstream (which is anonymous by design).
1226	- `policy.json` is `insecureAcceptAnything`: no signature is checked. It is
1227	  bounded by the loopback guard (only the bench's own registries are reached),
1228	  not by the policy.
1229	
1230	**Tests.** The two doors are tested with the "helper process" pattern
1231	(`helper_process_test.go`): a one-line shell shim named `kubectl` or `skopeo` is the
1232	only thing on PATH and re-runs the test binary, which records its arguments,
1233	environment and the files it was pointed at (authentication file, policy,
1234	`registries.conf`, read while they exist), answers as the test asked and exits or
1235	hangs. `TestSkopeoAgainstFakeRegistry` runs the real skopeo against
1236	`fakeregistry_test.go`, an in-process OCI registry on the loopback with an
1237	optional Basic challenge (skipped without skopeo): HTTP fallback, credentials from
1238	the authentication file, `--preserve-digests` byte for byte, and the error kinds.
1239	None of it needs the cluster or `requireBench`; the source guards (below) list why
1240	each such test is exempt.
1241	
1242	## The upstream lifecycle (`upstream.go`, DEVDESK-540)
1243	
1244	`UpstreamState` is `UpstreamMissing` < `UpstreamCut` < `UpstreamStarting` <
1245	`UpstreamReady`. Neither function runs a preflight: the callers do (`Deploy`,
1246	then the seed, `RunPreflight(OpSeed)`).
1247	
1248	`ReadUpstream(ctx, runner, p)` reads only: `get deployment bench-upstream -n <ns>
1249	-o json` (the object by name, never the list), then, when one replica is wanted,
1250	`get pods -n <ns> -l app.kubernetes.io/name=bench-upstream -o json`. A Deployment
1251	that is not there (`NotFound`) is Missing; zero replicas is Cut, even while an old
1252	pod is still terminating; otherwise a pod that is not terminating and whose `Ready`
1253	condition is `True` is Ready, else Starting (a pod that fails to pull is Starting,
1254	not an error: diagnosing is the wait's job). A failed read is a `*BenchError`
1255	classified like every other call.
1256	
1257	`EnsureUpstream(ctx, runner, clock, p, out)` reads first and writes at most once:
1258	
1259	| State read | Does |
1260	|---|---|
1261	| Missing | an error naming `bench-upstream` and `mise run nexus-bench:up` (`Deploy` applies the Deployment); no write |
1262	| Ready | nothing: no write, no wait |
1263	| Starting | no write; the wait |
1264	| Cut | `kubectl scale deployment/bench-upstream --replicas=1 -n <ns>` once (a failed scale is classified and not retried), then the wait |
1265	
1266	A custom upstream (`!p.UpstreamIsBench()`) is refused before any call, with an
1267	error that names `NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_URL`: the bench scales the upstream it
1268	deploys and nothing else. The wait is the one of `Deploy` without the hosts: a
1269	round (`round()`, shared) reads the pods of the upstream and the claim
1270	`bench-upstream-data`, diagnoses them with `upstreamWorkload()`, then ends on a
1271	ready pod, on the deadline (`Params.Timeout`, within one interval; a `Deadline`
1272	that cites the pod and names `NEXUS_BENCH_TIMEOUT`, or the pending reading that
1273	was still there) or sleeps `upstreamPollInterval` (2 s: a registry starts in
1274	seconds, and nothing is probed). A cancelled context is returned as is.
1275	`CutUpstream`, the recycling of the storage and the `OpCut`, `OpRestore` and
1276	`OpReset` preflights come with NX-02b.
1277	
1278	**Rights.** `up` gained, after its fourteen, patch `deployments/scale`, create
1279	`pods/portforward` and get `services` (namespace); `seed` asks get `deployments`,
1280	list `pods`, get `pods`, get `services`, create `pods/portforward` and patch
1281	`deployments/scale`. `kubectl port-forward svc/bench-upstream` fetches the Service,
1282	lists the pods of its selector, gets the pod it picks, then posts to
1283	`pods/portforward`: that is why `get services` and `get pods` are asked, on top of
1284	`list pods`.
1285	
1286	## The seed (`seed.go`, DEVDESK-542, NX-02a)
1287	
1288	`Seed(ctx, SeedDeps{Runner, Forwarder, Copier, Clock, Store}, baseURL, p, out)`
1289	puts the data set (D-I, `Dataset()`) in place and returns it as a `SeedResult`
1290	(digests filled, `PullThrough` true exactly for the images cached by
1291	`docker-proxy`). It never scales, applies or writes to Nexus (every request it
1292	sends is a `GET` as `admin`), and it runs no preflight: the caller does.
1293	
1294	**Order.**
1295	
1296	1. The stored credentials (`adminFromStore`, then the `bench-pull` password): a
1297	   missing one is `ProvisionFailed` that says to run `mise run nexus-bench:up`,
1298	   before any kubectl call or request.
1299	2. The upstream: a custom `NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_URL` is `SeedFailed` (the proxy
1300	   would not read what the seed pushes); then `ReadUpstream`: cut (`the upstream
1301	   is cut`, run `nexus-bench:restore-upstream`), missing (run `up`) and starting are
1302	   `SeedFailed` with no write and no copy. Bringing a cut upstream back is NX-02b.
1303	3. The OCI layout of the whole data set in a folder made under `TMPDIR`
1304	   (`os.MkdirTemp`), removed when Seed returns; the layout reference of an image is
1305	   its index in `Dataset()`, so the two `shared/base` images do not mix.
1306	4. One port-forward to `svc/bench-upstream:5000`, stopped by a `defer` on every
1307	   path. Seed checks itself that its address is `127.0.0.1:<port>` before any call
1308	   to the copier. The upstream images are pushed, in the order of `Dataset()`, with
1309	   no credentials; the forward is stopped before the next phase.
1310	5. The `docker-hosted` images, in order, with `admin` (`nexusImageRef`).
1311	6. The pull-through: the `PullThrough` images are copied from `docker-proxy` to a
1312	   throwaway `dir:` folder with `bench-pull`. `docker-proxy` is listed first by
1313	   REST; an image it lists is not pulled again unless the listed digest differs
1314	   from the data set's.
1315	7. The listings, by REST as `admin`: `docker-proxy` must hold exactly the
1316	   `PullThrough` images and `docker-hosted` exactly the hosted ones (name and tag
1317	   are enough: a component listed without a digest counts as present; a digest it
1318	   does list must be the one of the data set, else it is a failure). A missing one is
1319	   waited for, by `Clock`, 30 s at most (2 s polls, the same bound for both
1320	   repositories, H-COMPONENTS), then `SeedFailed`. A component outside the data set
1321	   fails at once, without waiting, with `<repo> holds images outside the dataset`
1322	   and `run mise run nexus-bench:reset`.
1323	
1324	**Idempotence.** An image is copied only when `ManifestDigest` at its destination
1325	differs from the digest of the data set. Absent means `errors.Is(err,
1326	errImageAbsent)`: `ManifestDigest` (through `inspectFailure`) puts that sentinel in
1327	the chain of its error only when `isImageAbsent(stderr)` proves the absence
1328	(`manifest unknown`, `name unknown`, `NAME_UNKNOWN`, `not found` or a whole-word
1329	`404`, any case) and the output is not one `classifySkopeo` reads as an unreachable
1330	or refusing registry (a refusal that quotes a 404 proves nothing). No manifest
1331	printed, a manifest above 4 MiB, an unreachable or refusing registry, an
1332	interrupted call and any unclassified output carry no sentinel: every other read
1333	error stops the seed. Every `Copy` carries
1334	`--preserve-digests`. A second run copies nothing (CA6).
1335	
1336	**F9.** `mirror/uncached` is never read through `docker-proxy` or `docker-group`:
1337	a read caches it, and only `reset` removes it. Seed pulls through the proxy only
1338	the `PullThrough` images and never reads the group.
1339	
1340	**Credentials.** None for the upstream, `admin` for `docker-hosted`, `bench-pull`
1341	for `docker-proxy`. No password reaches `out`, an error or an argv. Every failure
1342	is a `*BenchError`; a `*BenchError` of a door keeps its kind and gains the step
1343	(`copying api:1.0.0 to docker-hosted: ...`), any other error becomes an
1344	`Unclassified` one that keeps the cause for `errors.Is` and prints none of it. A
1345	cancelled context is returned as is (`errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)`). Output
1346	lines start with `seed: `; a nil writer is accepted.
1347	
1348	**References.** `nexusImageRef(p, repository, img)` is the one place that builds
1349	`127.0.0.1:<HTTPNodePort>/<repository>/<name>:<tag>`; `upstreamImageRef(local,
1350	img)` builds `<local>/<name>:<tag>`.
1351	
1352	**Still to settle on the bench (step 12).** H-PATH: that the instance routes a
1353	docker client by repository path on the HTTP NodePort (if not, only
1354	`nexusImageRef` changes). H-PUSH: that a push of the layout to `docker-hosted`
1355	with `--preserve-digests` keeps the manifest digest. H-COMPONENTS: that a Docker
1356	component is one image tag whose manifest asset checksum is the digest (a component
1357	without one is accepted), that the listing shows up within 30 s, and that a
1358	repository with no such image answers `manifest unknown` or `NAME_UNKNOWN` (what
1359	`isImageAbsent` reads; any other wording stops the seed instead of being copied over).
1360	
1361	## Still to come
1362	
1363	**Step 12 (the real bench).** The versioned `descriptor.json` is still schema 1:
1364	it is regenerated on the real bench, after `up` seeds it, with the proxy, the
1365	upstream and the data set (and `LoadDescriptor` refuses it until then). The

1371

```bash
go test ./...
```

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

63	// account (/nexus-data/admin.password). ok is false, without an error, when the
64	// file does not exist, which is the normal state once the password has been
65	// changed.
66	type InitialPassword interface {
67		Read(ctx context.Context) (password string, ok bool, err error)
68	}

70	// Provision brings a running Nexus to the state the bench needs and returns
71	// what it read from the instance. It is idempotent: every object is read, then
72	// created when absent or replaced when present, so a second run changes nothing
73	// and a run after a hand edit puts the bench back. baseURL is the REST origin
74	// (scheme, host and port, no path).

81	func Provision(ctx context.Context, baseURL string, ip InitialPassword, store SecretStore, p Params, out io.Writer) (ProvisionResult, error) {

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()

```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:

    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName

    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file

    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

content.content: 101:**D158 — DEVDESK-505 (NX-02a): the bench seeds a registry upstream inside its namespace, fed by a dataset generated in Go and pushed by skopeo, and cuts it by scaling to zero. Decided (user, archived 2026-11-17; plan `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-505-plan.md`, drafted there under this number; Q1 to Q4 settled as recommended, except where stated): (1) The client is the host's `skopeo` (1.18.0 when planned; not pinned by mise), run as a process by `skopeo.go` with a cleaned environment and an explicit policy; a missing binary is `SkopeoMissing`. The bench does not measure Nexus with the client that populated it. (2) The images are generated in Go at seed time as OCI layouts in a temporary directory: uncompressed layer tar, sorted entries, zero timestamps, no `created` in the config, so the digests are stable and pinned in a golden file. A `layerGzip` constant switches the layer to gzip, without name or date, if Nexus refuses uncompressed layers (H-LAYER). Nothing is committed as a binary and nothing comes from the network. (3) The upstream is a `registry:3.0.0` Deployment `bench-upstream` in the namespace, with PVC `bench-upstream-data` (kept across a cut, deleted only by `reset`) and a ClusterIP Service `bench-upstream:5000`. The Deployment manifest carries no `replicas`, so `kubectl scale` owns that field and server-side apply never fights it: a cut scales to 0, a restore to 1. The development machine reaches the upstream by `kubectl port-forward` on loopback, for the seed only. No NodePort: a writable registry is not exposed to the LAN. The PVC is read by name, not by label (this corrects a latent NX-01 bug). (4) The hosted repository is seeded through path routing on the HTTP port (`127.0.0.1:<HTTPNodePort>/docker-hosted/...`). (5) TLS verification is disabled only for references whose host is `127.0.0.1` or `::1`, and only with a mandatory path. `seed` refuses a `--rest-host` that is not loopback. Credentials go through a temporary authfile (`0600` in a `0700` directory), never in argv. (6) The dataset is fixed in `dataset.go` and described in the descriptor: `api:1.0.0` and `api:1.1.0`, `team/api:1.0.0` and `tools/cli:0.1.0` in hosted; `shared/base:1.0` in hosted and in the upstream, with different content and digests; `mirror/cached:1.0` in the upstream, pulled once through the proxy; `mirror/uncached:1.0` in the upstream, never pulled. Each image carries a `org.devdesk.nexus-bench.source` label. (7) Absence is proven by a sentinel, `errImageAbsent`, returned only on a registry "manifest unknown"; any other failure stays an error, so an unreachable registry is never read as an empty one. (8) An unlisted digest is accepted. (9) Preflight checks the subresources the code uses (`kubectl auth can-i --subresource`: `deployments/scale`, `pods/portforward`), correcting an NX-01 defect that checked `pods/exec`. (10) `up` is extended: deploy Nexus and the upstream, bring the upstream to one ready replica, provision (the proxy is created and joins the group), seed, then write the descriptor, and only after full success. `seed` alone seeds. (11) The descriptor moves to schema 2 (`registryAccess`, `upstream`, `dataset`); `LoadDescriptor` rejects version 1. Rejected: a native Go registry client (it would share the bias of the client being measured); a public image from Docker Hub (network, mutable tags); an unauthenticated NodePort for the upstream (a writable registry on the LAN); `emptyDir` with reseeding (ad hoc content lost at each cut). (12) The story is split: NX-02a is DEVDESK-505 (upstream, proxy created, seed, descriptor; CA1, CA2, CA3, CA5, CA6); NX-02b is DEVDESK-534 (cut and restore, reset, proxy unblock, repository deletion; CA4, CA7). Why: one client and one dataset for every later measure, without a cluster-wide exposure, and a cut that the proxy cannot mistake for an empty registry. No separate ADR: the decision is local to the bench and reversible. **Reserves:** H-PATH, H-PUSH, H-LAYER, H-PROXYHTTP, H-DNS, H-UPRUN and H-COMPONENTS are **not lifted**: the bench no longer exists, so step 0 (probes on the existing bench) and step 12 (first real run) are still to do. Until then they are assumptions. The duplicate `shared/base:1.0` having two digests is also an assumption. `descriptor.json` is still versioned at schema 1 in the repository. **Plane:** DEVDESK-505 (NX-02a), DEVDESK-534 (NX-02b). Sources: `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-505-plan.md`, `internal/nexusbench/`, `docs/product/nexus-support/stories.md` (NX-02); D157.**

content.text:
Tout est vert : `up` va au bout sur le banc réel, le jeu de données est en place et `status` est propre. J'ai trouvé deux écarts non prévus (SSRF et routage par chemin), tous deux corrigés dans le provisioning.

Je n'ai rien committé. Je n'ai pas lancé `down`, ni touché au namespace ni au cluster hors `nexus-bench`.

**Étape 1 — SSRF**
- `/service/rest/v1/security/ssrf-protection` est un GET/PUT de `{enabled, allowedIPs[], allowedDomains[]}`.
- Le banc démarre avec `enabled:true` et les deux listes vides.
- Le réglage minimal est d'ajouter `bench-upstream.nexus-bench.svc.cluster.local` à `allowedDomains`. La protection reste active et aucun autre hôte n'est autorisé. Un nom de Service est stable, contrairement à une ClusterIP.
- Cela a suffi : le proxy est créé du premier coup.
- Dans `Provision`, l'étape `ensureUpstreamAllowed` passe avant la création du proxy :
  - Elle est idempotente : aucun PUT si l'hôte est déjà autorisé, comparaison insensible à la casse.
  - Elle garde les entrées existantes et envoie des tableaux, jamais `null`.
  - Elle ne bascule jamais la protection, et ne fait rien si elle est désactivée ou si l'endpoint renvoie 404.
  - Elle ne s'applique qu'à l'amont du banc. Pour une URL personnalisée, le refus devient une erreur `ProvisionFailed` qui nomme `NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_URL` et l'endpoint à modifier (nouveau verdict `APIError.RemoteURLPrivate`).

  allowed. Both are consequences of the design, not changes to it (D158 (3), (4),
  (13) in `docs/backlog.md`).

EOF

Pour les points 1, 3 et 4, les tests ont été écrits avant le code, mais je n'ai pas observé leur échec avant d'implémenter. Je suis passé directement du test au code.

1. **Libellés de `privateUpstreamError`** (`internal/nexusbench/provision.go`)
   - Banc dont l'amont est refusé malgré l'autorisation : la cause dit que l'amont devrait être autorisé. Le check renvoie à `/service/rest/v1/security/ssrf-protection` (endpoint absent, ou `allowedDomains` sans l'hôte). Aucun conseil « unset ».
   - URL personnalisée : le conseil « laissez `NEXUS_BENCH_UPSTREAM_URL` non défini » est conservé.
   - Deux tests couvrent les deux cas.
2. **Tests renforcés** (`internal/nexusbench/provision_ssrf_test.go`)
   - `TestProvisionSSRFSettingsRefusedFailsWithTheAccountHint` vérifie maintenant l'indice (`bench account`, `admin password`, `nexus-bench:down`).
   - `TestProvisionDoesNotAllowACustomIPUpstream` vérifie qu'il n'y a ni PUT sur ssrf-protection ni élargissement des listes.
3. **B1, défense en profondeur**
   - Nouvelle fonction `allowableUpstreamHost(p)` : `validateNamespace` d'abord, puis l'URL doit être sans identifiants et d'hôte exactement `bench-upstream.<ns>.svc.cluster.local`. L'erreur ne reprend aucune partie de l'URL.
   - Tests : un namespace réservé (`kube-system`) est refusé sans aucun appel à ssrf-protection ; une table de 8 cas couvre la fonction.
4. **B2, champs inconnus préservés**
   - Les réglages SSRF sont lus et renvoyés en `map[string]json.RawMessage`. Seul `allowedDomains` change, plus `allowedIPs` quand il vaut `null` ou est absent (envoyé en `[]`), car le faux Nexus refuse un tableau nul.
   - Le type `ssrfSettings` n'existe plus que côté test.
   - Le faux Nexus garde et renvoie les champs inconnus. Un test vérifie qu'un champ objet et un champ liste survivent au PUT.
5. **B3, doc** (`docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md`)
   - Nouvelle puce NX-02a dans « Residual risks » : `pathEnabled` expose docker-hosted et docker-proxy par chemin sur le NodePort HTTP, y compris en pull anonyme ; un tiers du LAN peut déclencher des fetchs du proxy vers `bench-upstream` ; l'entrée `allowedDomains` reste dans l'instance jusqu'à un reset ; renvoi vers D158 (3), (4), (13).
   - L'étape 8a du provisioning est mise à jour (map brute, hôte exact, messages distincts).
